text:
maria: FYI started sanity runs for Galatea-9B (int6 vs int4) on our long-email+code summarization slice. posting raw-ish observations now.
omar: nice — what's the baseline (fp16) perf and unit costs?
kai: baseline fp16 p95 latency ~420ms, tokens per request ~850 (avg). quality: abstractive ROUGE-L 48.3, exact-code-snippet-preservation 92.1%.
omar: and int6 / int4? numbers pls.
kai: int6 p95 ~360ms, ROUGE-L 47.9 (-0.4), snippet-preserve 90.8 (-1.3). int4 p95 ~330ms, ROUGE-L 46.0 (-2.3), snippet-preserve 86.5 (-5.6). cpu/gpu mem stable, kv-cache hit unchanged.
maria: cost calc quickie (we used $0.08 / 1k tokens fp16, $0.03 / 1k tokens int6, $0.015 / 1k tokens int4 for infra econ):
```
avg_tokens = 850
requests_per_1k = 1000
fp16_cost = (850 * 1000 / 1000) * 0.08 = $68
int6_cost  = (850 * 1000 / 1000) * 0.03 = $25.5
int4_cost  = (850 * 1000 / 1000) * 0.015 = $12.75
```
maria: so int6 ~2.7x cheaper than fp16, int4 ~5.3x cheaper. tradeoffs are visible in the code-snippet metric.
sam: from product/GTN POV we care about "does the user notice?" — for long-email summarization the 1.3% snippet drop for int6 seems low risk. int4 losing ~5-6% snippet preservation may be visible for dev-focused features.
omar: agree. we should SLO-intent route: default int6, fallback to fp16 for high-value or flagged requests, and only route to int4 for cost-heavy low-risk flows (e.g., quick gist, low-fidelity preview).
kai: also saw prompt-length sensitivity: for >2k tokens int4 errors spike. For <1k tokens int4 is okayish. suggests routing by input token count + snippet-detection heuristics.
maria: flagging an ops note: int4 showed transient higher variance on p99 when KV cache cold. p99 increased to ~980ms in 3/50 runs. not catastrophic but noticable.
ops-bot: deploy-check: canary pool (galatea-9b-int6) healthy (5/5 backends), traffic 2%->10% ramp OK.
sam: proposed GTN language: "Galatea-9B (int6): 2.7x cost improvement vs fp16 with near-identical summarization fidelity for general users. Int4: ultra-cost option for lightweight previews; may degrade code snippet fidelity." want me to draft?
maria: please. also include routing guidance: "route by token length, snippet-detection, and customer tier."
omar: rollout plan suggestion: 1) internal canary (2-5%), 2) customer pilot for non-critical flows, 3) enable as default for free-tier/preview with opt-out for devs, 4) monitor snippet-preserve and rollback if monthly regression >1.5% vs baseline.
kai: adding instrumentation: include a tiny synthetic test that checks snippet-preserve on every release (sample set of 50 code-heavy emails) and alert if fail rate >3%.
maria: ok, action items: @kai add synthetic probe, @omar wire routing flag by token-length + snippet-heuristic, @sam draft GTN copy and risk notes, I'll run extended int6 production shadow for 48h and push metric dump.
sam: I'll coordinate docs + one-pager for sales (clear bullets on expected regressions and recommended fallbacks).
maria: thanks — will post results when shadow finishes (~48h). :thumbsup:
